name: Genoveil
description: A gene expression regulator designed to maintain the intended phenotypic output of cosmetic and functional geneware modifications by binding to modified gene promoter regions and suppressing epigenetic drift. Without stabilization, geneware modifications — engineered bioluminescence, pigmentation, structural modifications, decorative appendages — can drift in expression over months, producing unintended features or losing intended ones. Genoveil is the standard maintenance medication for anyone carrying active geneware.
effects: locks geneware expression to intended phenotype
prevents epigenetic drift in modified loci
maintains stability of structural geneware modifications
extends the effective lifespan of cosmetic modifications
side_effects: may suppress beneficial epigenetic adaptations alongside drift
occasional color-cast shift in natural pigmentation
reduced adaptability of immune genetic response
mild hormonal fluctuation in first month
long-term use associated with brittle nail and hair in some users
cultural_context: Geneware is fashion in GLMZ — bioluminescent skin traceries, engineered eye colors, functional tails, modified ear structures. It's also expensive to install and meaningless if it drifts. Genoveil is the unglamorous maintenance behind the glamour. People who can't afford it watch their modifications slowly become something unintended — a source of deep anxiety for those whose identity is tied to their aesthetic modifications. On the Shelf, people skip it and live with the drift, sometimes with striking results.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 socialite's bioluminescent geneware has begun expressing a pattern she didn't commission — and the pattern matches something encoded in a classified Helix research project she was never supposed to see.

A community on the Shelf has collectively stopped taking Genoveil, allowing their shared geneware modifications to drift together — developing a unique emergent aesthetic that is becoming a cultural identifier and a target for Lazarus's IP enforcement division.
Someone is deliberately dosing a geneware artist with a Genoveil analog that causes accelerated drift, destroying their signature modifications before a major commission.
